Title: Dog capture followed SOP, says Klang mayor
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Royal Klang City Council (MBDK) has denied breaching standard operating procedures (SOPs) during a stray dog capture operation that resulted in the death of a dog at Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Klang, last week.
Mayor Datuk Abd Hamid Hussain said the incident occurred after a person claiming to be the dog's owner disrupted the operation.
He said the council followed the Housing and Local Government Ministry's approved procedures, which allow the use of catch poles (loops) and nets.
"Based on reports from our officers, the operation was conducted according to SOPs. We use loops or nets to capture stray dogs.
"That night, we successfully captured 12 dogs with the cooperation of residents. The incident happened while we were trying to catch the 13th dog.
"During a struggle with a resident who claimed to be the dog's owner, the animal became entangled in the catch pole and died," he told reporters at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly lobby today.
Hamid said anyone claiming ownership of a captured dog should follow the prescribed procedure to reclaim the animal after it had been impounded.
"Initially, the individual claimed ownership of the dog, but later said it did not. We will leave the matter to the police, and any further action will depend on the outcome of the investigation.
"So far, two council officers have had their statements recorded by the police," he said.
He acknowledged that public perceptions of stray dog capture methods differed but stressed that the safety of enforcement personnel and residents had to remain the priority.
"Stray dogs can be aggressive. We cannot capture them gently if doing so endangers our officers or allows the animals to escape," he said.
He said notices about the operation had been issued in advance through Residents' Associations, and the operation involved 11 council personnel assisted by about 50 residents.
He said the operation was carried out following numerous complaints about stray dogs roaming the area and posing a risk to public safety.
"We receive about 50 complaints involving stray dogs every month. The problem is particularly serious in the area, and our actions are based on these complaints," he said.
Hamid added that the council faced manpower shortages and had been unable to secure private contractors to carry out stray dog capture operations.
"Our enforcement team has fewer than 20 personnel, while complaints continue to increase and Klang covers a large area.
"Many stray dogs are found in industrial and residential areas and are usually active at night, making them more difficult to catch," he said.
The operation drew public attention after a person allegedly threatened enforcement officers with a knife and attempted to obstruct the operation.
South Klang police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey previously said the case is being investigated under Section 428 of the Penal Code for mischief by killing an animal.

Title: BN 'stabbed' PH in Negri Sembilan election, says Mujahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The outcome of the Negri Sembilan election represents a triumph of racial identity politics over the multiracial, values-based platform championed by Pakatan Harapan, Amanah deputy president and election director Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa said.
He claimed that voters in the state appeared to have chosen emotion and racial sentiment over the government's performance and track record.
"While we respect the voters' decision, we are also concerned that parties promoting narrow racial and religious identity narratives risk pushing the political climate towards greater volatility," he said in a statement.
Mujahid warned that growing distrust and animosity between different races and religions would further erode the stability and unity underpinning Malaysia's prosperity.
The Aug 1 election saw Barisan Nasional, which entered an electoral understanding with Perikatan Nasional, secure a two-thirds majority after winning a combined 25 seats.
The result unseated the PH state government, which had been in power since 2018.
The election also delivered major upsets for the coalition, with caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun losing the Linggi seat, while DAP secretary-general and Transport Minister Anthony Loke was defeated in Chennah, a seat he had held since 2013.
Mujahid also criticised BN, PH's partner in the federal unity government, over its cooperation with PN during the state election.
He said the political message became "murkier" as BN used its ministerial and official positions to campaign while simultaneously working with PN.
"BN's conduct in Negri Sembilan is regrettable for openly 'stabbing' its partner by dividing seats with PN to defeat the unity government in Negri Sembilan, which had been jointly formed before the state election," he said.
Mujahid said PH must recognise that its aspiration for unity had been overtaken by what he described as PN's "Malay-Islamic supremacy agenda".
He also accused BN of being willing to abandon the vision of a Malaysia free from racial prejudice for the sake of power.
He said PH now faces a "difficult, uphill path" and must look inward to identify its weaknesses and rebuild its strength ahead of the next general election.

Title: Sabah records RM105.5 billion trade in 2025 despite global headwinds - DOSM
Article:
KOTA KINABAU: Sabah's trade performance remained resilient despite global economic uncertainties, with total trade maintaining above RM100 billion for the fourth consecutive year in 2025, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
In its 2026 Sabah External Trade Statistics report, DOSM said the state recorded total trade of RM105.5 billion last year, although this represented a 2.1 per cent decline from the previous year.
Exports fell 5.9 per cent to RM57.7 billion from RM61.3 billion in 2024, while imports rose 2.8 per cent to RM47.8 billion from RM46.4 billion.
Sabah recorded a trade surplus of RM9.9 billion, although it was 33.3 per cent lower than the RM14.9 billion recorded in 2024.
Crude petroleum remained Sabah's top export commodity, valued at RM17.1 billion or 29.7 per cent of total exports, followed by palm oil at RM16.8 billion (29.2 per cent) and liquefied natural gas at RM4.6 billion (8.1 per cent).
However, exports of crude petroleum and palm oil declined by 19.6 per cent and 2.9 per cent respectively, while liquefied natural gas exports increased by 2 per cent.
For imports, refined petroleum products worth RM4.8 billion and manufactured fertilisers worth RM1.1 billion were the main imported commodities.
DOSM said Sabah's external trade statistics also included inter-regional trade transactions with Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak based on the physical movement of goods through entry and exit points in the state.
"From the perspective of major trading partners, Peninsular Malaysia remained Sabah's largest trading partner, with total trade valued at RM49.6 billion, representing 47.1 per cent of the state's total trade.
"China remained the second largest trading partner with a trade value of RM10.4 billion, followed by Thailand (RM4.4 billion), South Korea RM4.2 billion) and Japan (RM4 billion)," DOSM said in a statement.
Sabah's exports to Asean countries totalled RM11.2 billion, a 4.2 per cent decline from the previous year.
The Philippines was Sabah's largest export destination within Asean, with exports valued at RM3.9 billion or 34.5 per cent of total exports to the region, followed by Thailand at RM3 billion (26.4 per cent) and Vietnam at RM2.1 billion (18.6 per cent).
By sector, mining remained the largest contributor to Sabah's exports at RM23.2 billion, accounting for 40.2 per cent of total exports.
This was followed by agriculture at RM22.1 billion (38.3 per cent) and manufacturing at RM12.3 billion (21.3 per cent).
For imports by end use, intermediate goods made up the largest category at RM17.5 billion, accounting for 36.7 per cent of total imports.
This was followed by consumption goods at RM15.6 billion (32.6 per cent) and capital goods at RM7.3 billion (15.3 per cent).
Imports of consumption goods and capital goods increased by 13.2 per cent and 9.1 per cent respectively, while intermediate goods imports declined by 5.9 per cent.

Title: Azalina: FOI Bill to undergo clause-by-clause review
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Parliamentary Special Select Committee reviewing the Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill 2026 aims to complete its deliberations and submit recommendations before the next Dewan Rakyat sitting.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the bipartisan committee would begin its work tomorrow, with the scope of the Bill among issues expected to be scrutinised.
She said the committee would first determine its terms of reference before conducting a clause-by-clause review of the Bill.
"The first meeting is tomorrow and I will be chairing it. We have bipartisan participation through the select committee.
"Tomorrow's meeting will focus on the terms of reference.
"We hope to complete the select committee's recommendations before the next Dewan Rakyat sitting for the FOI Bill," she told reporters after the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) monthly assembly for August today.
Asked whether major revisions were expected, Azalina acknowledged that concerns had been raised over the scope of the proposed legislation.
"There are many concerns, especially regarding the scope of the Bill.
"If you observe comments from NGOs and certain groups, they have said the FOI should be much wider. We will evaluate those concerns tomorrow," she said.
On July 13, Azalina announced that t
he Bill would be referred to a Parliamentary Special Select Committee
for further scrutiny, saying the move would allow lawmakers from both sides of the House and stakeholders to conduct a comprehensive review of every provision before it is tabled again in Parliament.
The review comes amid concerns raised during stakeholder engagements on the proposed law.
On June 29, Prime Minister's Department Legal Affairs Division deputy director-general (Policy and Development) Datuk Dr S. Punitha revealed that
five states were initially reluctant
to support the Bill.
The Bill has also faced criticism from within the government bloc.
Six Pakatan Harapan lawmakers recently
called for major amendments
, describing the government's draft as inadequate and weaker than existing freedom of information enactments in Selangor and Penang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1MDB alleges Najib orchestrated US$5.64bil fraud as civil trial opens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) civil suit against Datuk Seri Najib Razak opened today, with the state investment fund alleging that the former prime minister orchestrated a "top-down" fraud that caused losses of about RM51.4 billion and abused his positions to direct the company's affairs.
1MDB's lawyer Datuk Lim Chee Wee, in his opening statement, said the plaintiffs would rely on documentary evidence and witness testimony to prove that Najib exercised control over the fund's management through fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and oversaw four major phases of fund misappropriation.
The plaintiffs, comprising 1MDB and four of its subsidiaries, alleged that Najib exploited his positions as prime minister, finance minister and chairman of 1MDB's board of advisers to direct the company's affairs.
Lim said Low, despite holding no official position in 1MDB, acted as Najib's proxy by issuing instructions on his behalf.
He alleged that the fraud resulted in funds being siphoned for the benefit of, among others, Najib, his wife Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, his stepson Riza Aziz, Low and members of Low's family.
The plaintiffs are seeking to hold Najib and several former members of 1MDB's management accountable for losses arising from what they described as four phases of the alleged fraud — the Good Star, Aabar, Tanore and Options Buyback phases — involving the alleged misappropriation of about US$5.64 billion.
The seven co-defendants are Geh Choh Heng, former 1MDB general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Wan, Tang Keng Chee, Vincent Koh Beng Huat, Radhi Mohamad, Kelvin Tan Kay Jin and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil.
Lim said the alleged losses comprised US$1.83 billion in the Good Star phase, US$1.367 billion in the Aabar phase, US$1.591 billion in the Tanore phase and US$856.3 million in the Options Buyback phase.
The plaintiffs also told the court that the civil action followed Najib's conviction in the 1MDB criminal trial, in which he was found guilty on Dec 26 last year of four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering.
Lim argued that, by virtue of his positions as prime minister, finance minister and controller of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc), the sole shareholder of 1MDB, Najib exercised control over the company's directors and management, making him a shadow director under the Companies Act.
The plaintiffs further alleged that Najib initiated and facilitated fraudulent transactions before attempting to conceal them by dismissing senior public officials, including the deputy prime minister and attorney-general, and classifying the Auditor-General's Report on 1MDB under the Official Secrets Act.
Lim said documentary evidence would show that the alleged fraud followed a common pattern, with major projects or transactions first approved, substantial funds subsequently raised through borrowings or investments, and the proceeds eventually siphoned through various entities.
The court was told that six witnesses are expected to testify during the trial: Kroll Advisory managing director Angela Barkhouse, investigations director Richard Templeman, former 1MDB chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi, former 1MDB general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Wan, 1MDB director Mohd Hisyamuddin Awang Abu Bakar and former Public Accounts Committee member Tony Pua.
The plaintiffs are seeking to hold Najib and the relevant co-defendants liable for fraud, negligence, breach of fiduciary duty, breach of trust, conspiracy, misfeasance in public office, unjust enrichment, and knowing receipt or constructive trust, among other reliefs.
Najib attended today's proceedings and was represented by Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus continues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cook charged with assaulting fiancée-to-be with helmet
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 22-year-old cook was charged at the magistrate's court here with assaulting his fiancée-to-be using a helmet after she allegedly went out with another man.
The accused, Amyrul Fitri Rahshidi Rosman, 22, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno.
According to the charge, he allegedly injured his 22-year-old fiancée-to-be using a helmet at the Batu Pahat market here at 3.30pm on July 30.
The charge was framed under Section 324 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years, a fine, or whipping, or any two of the punishments upon conviction.
The court allowed the accused bail of RM5,000 with additional conditions that he must report to the nearest police station on the 4th of every month and not harass the victim until the case is resolved.
The court fixed Sept 28 for mention for document submission and the appointment of legal counsel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Religious affairs minister to table Tabung Haji RCI findings in Dewan Rakyat next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan will present the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Tabung Haji (TH) at a special parliamentary sitting next week.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the special sitting, scheduled for Aug 11, was called under Standing Order 14(1)(i).
The rule allows a minister to present an official statement or briefing on matters of importance, urgency, or public interest.
"The minister will brief the House on the findings of the RCI report, as well as the measures and actions taken by the government to restore TH's financial position.
"Following the presentation, the session will be opened for debate. Once the debate concludes, the Religious Affairs Minister will reply to issues raised by members of Parliament," Johari said.
Last Thursday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said that the special sitting would be held next Monday following agreement from the Dewan Rakyat Speaker.
This is to allow MPs to examine the findings of the RCI and discuss the direction of institutional reforms for the national haj management body.
Earlier, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) published the 211-page RCI report on the management and operations of TH from 2014 to 2020.
The report contains various recommendations to strengthen governance and improve the institution's operations.
Among the key findings of the RCI was that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, compared with the net profit of RM3.4 billion reported in its financial statements.
The commission also identified several governance weaknesses, including excessive ministerial powers in appointments, overlapping roles between board members and senior management, and political influence in TH's administration.
Regarding a call by Pagoh MP Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin for the special sitting to be extended to two days, Johari said he had not received any official request on the matter.
"I have not received any official request from anyone regarding the proposal," Johari said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alibaba unveils its most capable AI model to date, not far behind Moonshot's in size
Article:
BEIJING: China's Alibaba on Monday unveiled what it said is its largest and most capable artificial-intelligence model, the Qwen3.8-Max, which is not far behind in size when compared with an offering from domestic rival Moonshot AI launched last month.
Chinese tech companies — a huge force in open-weight AI models globally — are locked in a fierce and fast-moving battle to build more powerful systems without making them prohibitively expensive to run.
Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4 trillion parameters, the numerical settings a model learns from data and uses to recognise patterns, generate answers, and carry out tasks. Moonshot's Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters.
A higher figure does not automatically make a model better, but it has become a closely watched measure of the scale of the computing and data behind advanced AI systems.
Chinese tech companies are keen to publish parameter count to help their models gain traction among the developer community. Their models tend to be open-weight, meaning the underlying learned settings that allow developers to run or adapt the system are available for download.
By contrast, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google do not publish parameter count for their closed-source models.
Qwen3.8-Max was unveiled on crowdsourced, model-comparison platform Arena.AI, where it immediately became the highest-ranking Chinese model in terms of text models, though it still lags Claude Fable 5 and three Opus variants which are all from Anthropic.
But on Arena.AI's leaderboard for AI models that analyse images and other visual material, Qwen3.8-Max ranked second globally, only behind a Claude Fable 5 variant.
Both Qwen3.8-Max and Kimi K3 can handle text, images and video, and process up to 1 million tokens at a time.
Tokens are chunks of data, often parts of words or short words, and a big figure means the model can take in large amounts of material in one go, such as long legal files, a large software codebase or hundreds of pages of documents.
Alibaba said its model uses a "mixture-of-experts" design, which divides work among specialised parts of the system instead of switching on the entire model for every request. Only 95 billion parameters are used at a time, reducing costs and response delays.
The tech giant said the model completed a software-engineering project in 16 days.
The Qwen3.8-Max is due to be released next week through Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio platform.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Xin Hwa faces going concern warning from auditor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Xin Hwa Holdings Bhd has come under a going concern warning after its external auditor flagged material uncertainty over its ability to continue operating, with current liabilities exceeding current assets.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, Xin Hwa said PKF PLT had issued a modified audit opinion highlighting the going concern uncertainty in its audit of the company's financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026.
The auditors drew attention to the company's liabilities that exceeded its assets by RM41.69 million.
"This condition indicates that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the group's ability to continue as a going concern.
"The appropriateness of the going concern basis of accounting is dependent on the group's ability to generate and sustain future profitability and cash flows from its operations, the successful disposal of a parcel of vacant industrial leasehold land, and continued availability of banking facilities and financial support from the group's financial institution lenders," it said.
Xin Hwa said it had implemented measures to address the matter such as the disposal of two parcels of vacant industrial land in Pasir Gudang, Johor.
The company is also focused on the collection of long-standing receivables by conducting a thorough review of all receivables to identify the root causes of delayed payments, taking action on overdue receivables and reviewing its credit control policy.
Additionally, Xin Hwa said it had significantly reduced and deferred non-crucial capital expenditure during the current financial year.
The company said it had achieved a significant turnaround in its financial performance during the current financial year, recording a net profit of RM3.7 million compared with a net loss of RM11.3 million in the preceding financial year.
"This improvement was driven by higher revenue, improved operational efficiency, and ongoing cost optimisation initiatives," it added.
Trading in Xin Hwa was suspended on Monday from 9am until 10am the same day.
The counter last traded at 15 sen, with a market capitalisation of RM38.35 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand tightens border security after Tak Bai shootout
Article:
TUMPAT: Thai authorities have tightened security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following a shootout in Tak Bai yesterday that left two policemen dead and three others injured.
Narathiwat provincial police commander Major General Prayong Kotsakha said police, military personnel and local authorities were mobilised to secure the area and prevent the suspect from escaping.
"Soon after the incident, I directed border agencies to step up security operations along our border with Malaysia.
"Security personnel have been instructed to strengthen surveillance and block possible escape routes, particularly along the border," he said.
Prayong said a manhunt was ongoing, with investigators and forensic teams deployed to gather evidence at the scene.
Meanwhile, checks along the Golok River in Pengkalan Kubor today found that cross-border activities continued as usual despite the heightened security measures.
The movement of people and boats along the river was observed to be normal.
It was reported yesterday that
two Thai police officers were killed
and three others injured in an exchange of gunfire with a man during an anti-drug trafficking operation in Tak Bai.
Initial investigations found the suspect fled towards an oil palm plantation. Police have cordoned off the village area to search for him.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt finalising rail law amendments to raise cable theft fines to RM100,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is finalising amendments to rail transport laws to impose fines of up to RM100,000 on individuals who trespass and steal cables from rail facilities.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the proposal to increase the fine from the current RM1,000 is expected to be tabled in the next parliamentary session.
"We will amend this law to reach RM100,000 for each offence... currently in the process and God willing, perhaps by the end of this year in the next session, a stricter amendment to the law will be brought to this House," he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Negara today.
He was responding to a question from Senator Datuk Dr Mohd Hatta Md Ramli regarding government mitigation measures to address travel disruptions caused by cable theft and to safeguard public transport.
Hasbi said the amendment to the law was urgent as existing penalties were deemed too lenient compared with the operational delays and heavy financial losses borne by rail operators.
The move was also driven by a surge in cable theft cases, which recorded total losses of RM50 million across the Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) network, Prasarana Malaysia Bhd, and the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
According to Hasbi, a total of 71 cable theft cases were recorded along the ECRL project with an estimated loss of RM4.06 million, while 13 cases of theft and equipment damage resulted in losses of RM0.69 million.
"This brings the total loss to RM4.75 million. Although the ECRL is still under construction and has not disrupted passenger travel, these incidents could affect the project schedule, including testing, commissioning, and operational preparations," he said.
To bolster ground security, Hasbi said the government is installing 1,146 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras along the railway line from Johor to the north of the country.
He added that KTMB has also acquired 20 scrambler motorcycles for the Auxiliary Police to enhance 24-hour patrols, alongside physical security measures such as securing high-risk manholes and deploying sniffer dog units.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Couple charged with abusing 9-year-old daughter
Article:
AYER KEROH: A lorry driver and his wife pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to charges of abusing their 9-year-old daughter, leaving her with swelling, bruises, welts and trauma.
The accused, aged 36 and 35, entered their pleas before judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah after the charges were read to them.
The male accused was charged with physically abusing his daughter at a house in Presint Selendang, Taman 1 Krubong, Melaka Tengah, at 7pm on July 19.
His wife, a housewife, was charged with committing a similar offence against the girl at the same location at 2pm on July 21.
It is understood the abuse allegedly occurred after the victim made her 6-year-old brother cry and failed to tidy her bedroom.
The charges were framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Nor Asnini and Muhammad Qayyum Ramlan offered bail at RM20,000 for each accused with additional conditions.
The unrepresented male accused pleaded for a lower bail, saying his income as a lorry driver was irregular, ranging between RM3,000 and RM4,000 monthly, and that he was the family's sole breadwinner.
His wife also sought lower bail, saying she was unemployed and depended on her husband's income to support the family's two children.
She told the court that the children had been unable to attend school while both parents were in police custody as she had previously managed their schooling arrangements.
Rohatul Akmar granted bail of RM10,000 with one surety for the male accused and RM9,000 for his wife.
The court also ordered both accused not to intimidate or interfere with prosecution witnesses, especially the victim, and to report to the nearest police station every month.
The case was fixed for mention on Sept 8 for the appointment of legal counsel and submission of documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US reaffirms commitment to rule of law in Indo-Pacific
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United States remains committed to sharing common legal values and principles with its allies and partners in the Indo-Pacific region to protect sovereign equality, safeguard sovereign rights and advance the interests of all nations.
US Pacific Command (USPACOM) Staff Judge Advocate Captain Dustin Wallace said the United States and its partners, including Asean countries, viewed the rule of law as a means to safeguard and protect rights, rather than using law as a tool to isolate, intimidate or coerce other nations.
"We at USPACOM are firmly committed to the rule of law, ensuring that we use our legal, shared legal values and shared legal principles with our allies and partners to protect sovereign equality, safeguard sovereign rights and advance the interests of all our nations," he said at a press conference held in conjunction with the USPACOM 37th International Military Law and Operations Conference (Milops) 2026 today.
He said one of the key challenges in international military law was the differing approaches among countries in how they used and applied legal principles.
"We see a challenge where some nations operate under a rule by law system, where they use law as a tool to isolate, intimidate and coerce," he said.
In contrast, Wallace said the United States and its allies and partners operated under a rule of law system, where legal principles were used to safeguard and protect rights.
Wallace said Asean remained critical to regional peace and security, with USPACOM continuing to support Asean centrality in the Indo-Pacific.
"We at USPACOM want to encourage Asean centrality, we want to help where we can, and we want to focus on the specific interests of the countries here in the Asean nations," he said.
He said USPACOM wanted to work with each Asean country based on their respective sovereign interests, while maintaining existing relationships and building new partnerships to strengthen regional peace, security and prosperity.
Wallace said the United States remained committed to security and stability in the South China Sea, with USPACOM continuing to maintain its presence in the region to deter aggression and destabilising activities.
Wallace said Washington remained committed to principles including freedom of navigation and commerce, which he described as shared values between the United States and its regional partners.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenager pleads guilty to abandoning newborn in bushes
Article:
TAWAU: A 15-year-old school dropout pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court here today to abandoning her newborn baby in bushes at Kampung Jawa Sentosa, Jalan Guru, last month.
The teenager entered her plea after the charge was read to her before magistrate Dayang Aidaku Amira Aminuddin.
According to the charge, she allegedly abandoned her newborn girl with the intention of dumping the child in bushes at Kampung Jawa Sentosa, Jalan Guru, at 4.30am on July 21.
The charge was framed under Section 317 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of seven years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
The court fixed Sept 7 for mention while waiting for the accused's medical and chemistry reports.
Prosecution officer Assistant Superintendent Nur Intan Jamrin prosecuted, while the unrepresented accused pleaded for a lighter sentence.
Based on the facts of the case, police received public information at 7am on July 21 regarding the discovery of a newborn baby girl beside a house near the SMK Tawau Teachers' Flat in Kampung Jawa.
A team from the Tawau district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Department subsequently arrested the accused at a house in Kampung Jawa Sentosa at 11.10am the same day.
Investigations revealed that the accused gave birth to the baby at 4.30am in bushes near the SMK Tawau Teachers' Flat before abandoning the child there.
The 3.1kg baby girl was rescued by members of the public around 6am and taken to Tawau Hospital for medical examination and treatment.
Following the discovery, police also detained a male SPM school-leaver and remanded him for four days to assist in investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jealousy lands lorry driver in court for assaulting wife
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 32-year-old lorry driver pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court here today to assaulting his wife by punching her in the mouth during a quarrel allegedly triggered by jealousy.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno questioned the accused on where he would stay if bail was granted, stressing that he could not live with his wife while the case was ongoing.
"If the court allows bail, where will you stay? The court cannot allow you to live in the same house with your wife for the time being," he said.
The accused told the court he would stay at his parents' house until the case was concluded.
The father of two children from a previous marriage was charged with punching, pulling and pushing his 40-year-old wife against a wall at a house in Parit Raja here at 10.30pm on July 29.
The offence was charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 326A, which provides for a jail term of up to one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both upon conviction.
Section 326A provides for a punishment of up to twice the maximum imprisonment term for an offence under Section 323.
Based on the police report, the incident occurred after the accused became jealous when his wife received a phone call from a male acquaintance.
The accused allegedly became enraged, splashed water on his wife's face, dragged her into a room and pushed her against a wall.
The incident was witnessed by the complainant's daughter, who intervened to stop the argument.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shazleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while the accused was represented by Kamarulariffin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
The court granted the accused bail of RM4,000 with one surety and ordered him to report to the nearest police station every month.
He was also barred from approaching or disturbing the victim until the case is concluded.
The case will be mentioned again on Sept 28 for document submission and appointment of counsel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jalaluddin clarifies absence at Negri Sembilan MB swearing-in ceremony
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has clarified that his absence at the menteri besar swearing-in ceremony at Istana Besar Seri Menanti yesterday was due to short notice.
Jalaluddin, who is the Pertang assemblyman, said he received the invitation from the state Protocol unit at 4.50am.
"It was last minute. I received it at 4.50am from Protocol. I opened and read it after Subuh prayers, but I had already arranged another event in my constituency that required my presence," he said when contacted today.
Jalaluddin was responding to queries over his absence at the appointment and swearing-in ceremony for the Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah, which triggered speculation on social media.
Yesterday, Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim took his oath as the new Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud and her sons, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Zain Al'Abidin.
Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, and Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan were also in attendance.
At a press conference yesterday, Ismail dismissed speculation regarding the absence of several assemblymen at the ceremony.
He emphasised that invitations to all assemblymen were issued by the State Secretary's Office, but the short notice meant some might have had prior commitments.
"There must have been valid reasons. The invitation was made by the State Secretary's Office to everyone. It is just that the notice was quite short," Ismail said.
Elaborating further, Jalaluddin said the key priority was that Barisan Nasional's agenda in Negri Sembilan had been realised.
"Negri Sembilan can now be governed effectively after being given a two-thirds mandate by the people in the state election last Saturday.
"Therefore, it is the responsibility of all of us as elected representatives, as the menteri besar, and as executive council members to ensure that all our manifestos promised to the people are fulfilled.
"Our governance must be enhanced multifold compared with Pakatan Harapan," said the former senior state executive council member.
Jalaluddin stressed that he felt no disappointment or despair because his main objective in the state election had been achieved.
"Now we have been given the mandate by the people, so why should I be disappointed or give up?
"I feel immensely grateful to Allah for this success," he said.
Earlier, it is believed that Jalaluddin's name was among three presented as candidates for Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar to Tuanku Muhriz by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during an audience at Istana Hinggap Negeri Sembilan on the night of the election results.
In the state election, Jalaluddin defeated two challengers, PH candidate Mohd Umry Abdul Khois and Bersatu candidate Mohd Faizal Fadli Mohd Idrus, with a majority of 2,790 votes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five Taiwanese charged with trafficking Cameroonian woman for forced labour
Article:
BUTTERWORTH:  Five Taiwanese citizens pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a human trafficking charge involving a Cameroonian woman for alleged forced labour last month.
The accused — Chien Te Hsi, 27; Liao Shao Wei, 36; Hung Min Hung, 35; Chao Jhih Ying, 35; and Tseng Wei Ting, 29 — entered their pleas before judge Roslan Hamid after the charge was read to them in Mandarin by a court interpreter.
They were charged with trafficking a Cameroonian woman for forced labour at a premises in Jalan Utara Berapit, Central Seberang Perai, at 7pm on July 16.
The offence under Section 12 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nadhirah Abdul Rahim prosecuted, while the accused were represented by lawyers R. Vikraman and Naveen Chandra Bose.
Earlier, the prosecution did not offer bail, citing that the accused had entered Malaysia without valid passports or travel documents.
The court granted the prosecution three weeks to verify the accused's travel documents and fixed Sept 1 for mention.
Previously, Penang police reported that a human exploitation and job scam syndicate was dismantled following several raids in Seberang Perai Tengah and the Northeast district on July 16.
During the operation, police rescued a 25-year-old Cameroonian woman believed to be a victim of exploitation.
A total of 29 foreigners comprising 20 men and nine women were also arrested after failing to produce valid travel documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chow: Penang PH to stay focused on governance
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) will remain focused on governing the state despite Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional's confidence in capturing Penang.
State PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the opposition was entitled to pursue its own electoral strategy, but the outcome would ultimately depend on voters.
He said claims that the BN-PN cooperation model could be replicated in Penang stemmed from the coalition's performance in other states, where demographic factors had influenced electoral results.
"I think this view was expressed following the success of the cooperation formula between BN-PN, particularly in Negri Sembilan, where they managed to win several seats.
"So naturally, they see it as a formula that can be applied in other state elections. Considerations such as the ethnic composition in the respective states will give them an advantage when presenting such cooperation to win voters' support. That is up to each side's strategy to achieve victory," he told reporters at his office in Komtar here today.
He was responding to remarks that the BN-PN cooperation formula could enable the coalition to wrest control of Penang in the next general or state election.
Chow, who is also Penang Chief Minister, said PH in Penang would continue to champion inclusive governance and development for all communities instead of engaging in identity-based politics.
"They can use whatever approach they want, including in Penang. In the end, it is up to the voters to decide.
"For Pakatan Harapan in Penang, we will continue the state's development agenda. We have always been an inclusive government that looks after the welfare of the people and develops the state for everyone.
"We hope voters, regardless of race or religion, will judge the state government's performance and return the mandate to us in the next general or state election," he added.
On concerns that PH was losing support among Malay and Chinese voters, Chow said it was too broad a conclusion.
He said DAP continued to enjoy a satisfactory level of support in the constituencies it held, while the combined strength of BN and PN would naturally consolidate their respective voter bases.
Asked whether Umno's position in the Penang government would be reviewed if the party formalised cooperation with PN, Chow said the matter had yet to be discussed.
He said Penang PH would hold a meeting on Aug 8 to receive reports from its committees as part of preparations for the next general or state election, and issues relating to Umno's position in the state administration could be discussed then.
On the stability of the state government, Chow said the political situation could change, and any decision on the administration's future would rest with the Penang and national PH leadership.
"Politics changes every day. We need to consider all possibilities.
"We leave it to the Penang PH leadership and the central PH leadership to determine the direction. I cannot make that decision on my own," he said.
Earlier, Chow announced that Penang would host the 15th Malaysian Scout Jamboree from Aug 29 to Sept 4 at Bandar Cassia, Batu Kawan, marking a return to the state that hosted the nation's first jamboree in 1966.
The event, themed "Tracing Heritage, Building the Future" with the sub-theme "60 Years of Uniting the Spirit of Scouting", reflects Penang's commitment to youth development and leadership.
More than 5,400 participants are expected, including 5,005 scouts and 468 international participants from 11 countries, including Sri Lanka, Indonesia, South Korea and Singapore.
The event is expected to be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SunCon lands RM1.02bil Johor data centre job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) has secured a RM1.02 billion contract for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing fit-out works of a data centre development in Johor.
SunCon, in a Bursa Malaysia filing today, said its subsidiary Sunway Construction Sdn Bhd had accepted a letter of award from a US-headquartered multinational technology corporation for the project.
The contract takes immediate effect, with construction scheduled for completion by the fourth quarter of 2027.
SunCon said the project is subject to normal construction-related risks, including fluctuations in material prices.
It added that these are expected to be mitigated by the group's experience in construction and data centre development.
SunCon said the contract is expected to contribute to the group's earnings from the financial year 2026 onwards.
Following the latest award, SunCon has secured RM5.8 billion worth of new orders so far this financial year, bringing its outstanding order book to RM10.4 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US committed to strengthening defence ties with Malaysia - Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United States will continue strengthening its close relations with Malaysia, including in the defence sector, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said this was among matters highlighted during a courtesy call by US Ambassador to Asean Kevin Kim in conjunction with the United States Pacific Command 37th International Military Law and Operations Conference (Milops) 2026 today.
"They said they will continue to give further attention to enhancing and strengthening the close relations between the two countries, including in the defence sector," he said when met after the meeting.
Khaled said the meeting only focused on strengthening existing ties and did not involve policy discussions.
He also received courtesy calls from Asean secretary-general Dr Kao Kim Hourn and Singapore Ministry of Defence Permanent Secretary Joseph Leong.
During his meeting with Kao, Khaled said they discussed challenges faced by Asean and efforts to strengthen the defence sector's role in upholding Asean Centrality, peace, stability and prosperity in the region.
He said the defence sector played an important role in supporting Asean's objectives and enhancing cooperation among member states.
Meanwhile, in his meeting with Leong, Khaled said Singapore had also expressed its commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Malaysia.
"The cooperation would not only involve bilateral relations but also encompass multilateral cooperation at the Asean level as well as through the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA)," he said.
The 37th Annual Milops Conference is being held in Kuala Lumpur from Aug 3 to 6, bringing together government officials and military representatives from more than 30 countries to discuss regional security challenges and enhance cooperation in military law and operations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother, boyfriend charged with murdering 5-year-old boy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: An Indonesian woman and her Bangladeshi boyfriend were charged in the magistrate's court here today with murdering a 5-year-old boy.
The victim was the Indonesian woman's son with her Rohingya husband, who died last year.
Sany, 34, and Dina Hayati, 30, nodded to indicate they understood the charge read before magistrate Noor Idayu Salim.
No plea was recorded as the offence falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The duo were jointly charged with murdering Ali Sahari Ali Juhar at the living room of a house at 7B, Level 2, Lintang Merak, Sungai Dua here at about 9.30am on July 23.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Ahmad Danial Amir Saad prosecuted, while the two accused were unrepresented.
Noor Idayu fixed Oct 6 for case mention pending submission of the chemist and post-mortem reports.
Earlier, the two arrived separately at the court complex before 9am in handcuffs.
They were previously remanded to assist investigations after the boy was found unconscious and later pronounced
dead
at Penang Hospital.
It is learnt that the child had bruises on his body when hospital staff examined him, prompting a report to be lodged and the arrests.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nestle Malaysia beats 2025 emissions goal ahead of schedule
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has reduced its greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) by 31 per cent from its 2018 baseline.
This surpasses its interim target of a 20 per cent reduction by 2025, advancing towards its goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
Nestle Malaysia said the achievement was driven by initiatives across its operations and supply chain.
This includes the transition to 100 per cent renewable electricity, manufacturing efficiency improvements, regenerative agriculture, sustainable sourcing practices and circular packaging programmes.
Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the milestone reflected years of collaboration across the company's operations and value chain.
"Reaching a 31 per cent reduction in GHG emissions is an important milestone, reflecting years of commitment by our teams and partners across Malaysia.
"While we are proud of this progress, we know there is still much more to do on our journey to Net Zero," he said.
Aranols added that sustainability remains integral to the company's operations, from energy use and sourcing practices to packaging, ecosystem restoration and community initiatives.
The announcement comes as Malaysia advances its climate commitments under its Nationally Determined Contribution, submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change in October 2025, which outlines the country's pathway towards net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.
According to Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, private sector participation would be crucial in achieving Malaysia's climate goals.
"Initiatives such as those undertaken by Nestle Malaysia show that emissions reductions can be successfully integrated into business operations while supporting long-term economic growth," he said.
Nestle Malaysia also reaffirmed its focus on packaging sustainability through measures such as reducing virgin plastic use, increasing recycled PET content and strengthening post-consumer waste recovery.
A key initiative is Nestle Kitar, the refreshed platform for Project SAVE (Segregate, Avoid, Value, Educate), which the company said is Malaysia's largest extended producer responsibility programme.
To date, the programme has recovered and recycled 50,000 tonnes of dry mixed waste, including 32,000 tonnes of plastics.
The company's sustainability efforts also extend to environmental restoration, with three million trees already planted nationwide under Project RELeaf.
Nestle Malaysia has committed to planting another three million trees by 2030 to support biodiversity conservation and climate resilience.
Having exceeded its 2025 emissions target, the company is now focused on achieving a 50 per cent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 as part of its pathway towards net zero by 2050.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 14.2 million Malaysians benefit from targeted RON95 subsidy, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 14.2 million of the 16.7 million eligible Malaysians have benefited from the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) targeted fuel subsidy programme, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the initiative involved the consumption of over 13.4 billion litres of RON95 fuel.
Amir Hamzah added that the unsubsidised RON95 price, which fluctuates according to market rates, applies only to non-eligible buyers, including non-citizens and those failing to meet Budi95 criteria.
"Based on actual Budi95 usage data from October 2025 to June 2026, fewer than one per cent of Budi95 users consistently consume more than 200 litres of RON95 per month.
"On average, RON95 consumption is around 100 litres per month," he told the Dewan Negara during the question-and-answer session today.
He was responding to a question from Senator Datuk Bobbey Ah Fang Bin Suan regarding annual cost savings from the targeted subsidy.
Amir Hamzah explained that based on current implementation, annual fiscal savings are estimated at between RM2.5 billion and RM4.0 billion, depending on global crude oil prices, exchange rate movements, and fuel consumption patterns.
Responding to a supplementary question from Senator Robert Lau Hui Yew on the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD) recommendation for Malaysia to phase out Budi95 over the medium term, Amir Hamzah said the government had already shifted from a blanket subsidy model.
"The Budi95 eligibility framework allows Malaysian citizens to receive subsidised RON95 for up to 200 litres, while non-citizens do not receive this subsidy. This has saved the government's fiscal space.
"We fully understand that the OECD has recommended the withdrawal of all subsidies, but we cannot do that in this country. What is important is that we provide subsidies in a targeted manner rather than making abrupt changes as suggested by the OECD," he said.
The France-headquartered OECD had recommended that Malaysia gradually eliminate fuel subsidies to strengthen its financial position as the country approaches high-income nation status.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teenager's murder trial over Bandar Utama school stabbing begins
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The murder trial of a 15-year-old boy accused of fatally stabbing his schoolmate at a school in Bandar Utama last year begins today.
The prosecution is expected to call the pathologist who conducted the 16-year-old victim's post-mortem examination as its first witness.
The victim's mother is also expected to testify, including identifying photographs of her late daughter and other exhibits.
Several teachers from the school are among the witnesses expected to take the stand today.
The trial before High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid is scheduled to run for eight days.
The teenager, who cannot be publicly identified or photographed as he is a minor, was brought to the courtroom from the Puncak Alam Correction Centre, a juvenile detention facility.
Proceedings are being held in camera.
According to the charge sheet, he is accused of murdering his schoolmate in the girls' toilet of SMK Bandar Utama Damansara (4) in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14 last year.
The victim was identified as Form Four student Yap Shing Xuen.
The charge carries the death penalty, or imprisonment of not less than 30 years and not more than 40 years, and 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death sentence cannot be imposed on a child at the time of the offence.
Instead, Section 97(2) stipulates that a person convicted of such an offence shall be detained at the pleasure of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong if the offence occurred in the Federal Territories, or the Ruler or Yang di-Pertua Negeri if it occurred in a state.
A three-month psychiatric assessment conducted by Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta director Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony concluded that the boy is fit to stand trial.
A total of 11 prosecution witnesses are expected to testify in the trial, including three child witnesses aged between 13 and 17, whose testimony will be governed by the Evidence of Child Witness Act 2007.
The boy is represented by lawyer Kitson Foong.
Deputy public prosecutors Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Azman appeared for the prosecution.
Lawyers Datuk Yasmeen Shariff and Jason Lim Jie Sheng are holding watching briefs for the Bar Council and the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia, respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official, government says
Article:
BANGKOK: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, a government spokeswoman said, amid concerns over the health of the 81-year-old.
The Nobel Peace Prize winner has been in detention since February 2021, when an elected civilian government led by her was ousted by Myanmar's military in a dawn coup, plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil.
Since then, Suu Kyi's exact whereabouts and health condition have been difficult to determine, with no foreign leader or envoy having publicly met her.
On Monday, Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw, government spokeswoman Khine Khine Soe said in a message via Telegram.
The ICRC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In two of the four photographs provided by the government spokeswoman, Suu Kyi — dressed in traditional Burmese attire — is seen meeting with Baecque in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room containing only two chairs and a desk.
In another photo, offering a rare glimpse inside what appears to be her residence, Suu Kyi is seen cutting a birthday cake inscribed with her name, with a clothes rack and storage boxes visible in the background. A fourth photograph is a close-up of the cake, inscribed with "Happy Birthday Aunty Suu 29.6.2026."
Reuters was not able to independently verify the location or the date on which the pictures were taken. No earlier version of the pictures was found posted online before Monday.
MOVE TO HOUSE ARREST
Suu Kyi has been serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted of multiple offences based on charges her allies said were politically motivated.
In late April, following a military-engineered election that allowed former junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to become Myanmar's president, authorities said she had been moved to house arrest.
Her sentence was also commuted by one-sixth as part of an amnesty for thousands of prisoners, which also saw the release of her ally, former president Win Myint.
But the new military-backed administration has so far been reluctant to provide access to Suu Kyi, including a May request by the Philippines to allow a special envoy of the regional Asean bloc to meet the detained leader.
Myanmar's junta said last December that Suu Kyi was "in good health", after her son told Reuters he had received little information about his ageing mother's condition and had not heard from her in years, fearing she could die without him knowing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amirudin urges fair debate over Selangor stray dog issue
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has urged all parties not to be selective in criticising the state government over the stray dog issue, stressing the need to balance public safety and animal welfare.
He said the state government would continue taking action against stray dogs but must consider the wider public interest.
"We will continue to take action against stray dogs, but the state government must act in the interest of the public.
Amirudin said the focus should be on finding a balance by preventing stray dogs from roaming freely and posing risks to residents, while also addressing animal welfare concerns.
"Do not be selective when making accusations," he said.
Amirudin was responding to claims that animal welfare was being prioritised over the safety of residents affected by stray dog attacks.
He was speaking after attending a gathering with civil servants at the Jubli Perak Auditorium in the State Secretariat Building here today.
Amirudin added that Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, had also raised the matter, advocating legal action against those who abuse animals.
"Do not be angry if there are people concerned about animal welfare, as we also look after human welfare," he said.
Earlier, a stray dog capture operation by the Royal Klang City Council in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah late last month went viral after a dog died during the operation.
The incident is now being investigated by police.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump attorney-general pick says has reached deal with senators after standoff
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US acting attorney general said on Sunday he had reached an agreement with lawmakers and issued an order officially scrapping a US$1.8 billion compensation fund that had led to a standoff over his Senate confirmation.
Todd Blanche's announcement came after the Senate Judiciary Committee pushed back a vote on advancing his nomination owing to his continuing dispute with Republican Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina.
Cornyn and Tillis have said they will withhold support for Blanche until the Trump administration rescinds plans for a controversial US$1.8 billion "anti-weaponisation" fund for people claiming they have been victims of politically motivated prosecutions.
"My team and I have met with committee members and senators over the past several weeks and addressed any concerns or outstanding questions," Blanche wrote on X.
"We have enjoyed good faith discussions, and as a result issue the following order and update with regard to the May IRS settlement," he added.
A signed order attached to Blanche's post said: "The Attorney General's May 18, 2026 Order establishing the Anti-Weaponisation Fund... is rescinded and shall have no force or effect.
"This Order establishes, beyond any doubt, that there is no Fund."
The Senate Judiciary Committee is now due to vote on Blanche's nomination on Tuesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BHEUU targets faster legal reforms, better access to justice
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Accelerating legal reform, digital transformation and improving access to justice are among key priorities under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister's Department Strategic Plan 2026-2030.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the roadmap was designed to position BHEUU as a leading force in legal and institutional reform to support national wellbeing.
"The strategic plan is not merely a planning document, but a shared commitment to build an organisation that is more efficient, innovative and focused on results," she said at the launch of the plan during the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) monthly assembly here today.
Azalina said the plan focused on three key priorities including driving responsive legal reforms, strengthening the implementation and delivery of legislation, and enhancing digital capabilities through technology, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI).
She added that the Strategic Digitalisation Plan 2026-2030 would simultaneously support organisational transformation through the adoption of smart technology to improve efficiency, speed up processes and strengthen public confidence in the legal system.
"Through the use of smart technology, we aim to improve service delivery, accelerate work processes and strengthen trust in the country's legal institutions," she said.
Azalina said the success of the plan would depend on effective implementation and the commitment of all BHEUU personnel.
She added that legal and institutional reform required close cooperation between departments and agencies, supported by a culture of collaboration, knowledge sharing and open communication.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maybank buys remaining Ageas stake for RM4.83bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is buying the remaining 30.95 per cent stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd from Ageas Insurance International NV for RM4.83 billion.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Maybank said it had entered into an implementation agreement with Ageas for the proposed acquisition, which is subject to approval from Bank Negara Malaysia.
Maybank Ageas is the holding company of Etiqa's operations in Malaysia and Singapore, offering conventional life and general insurance as well as family and general takaful products through multiple distribution channels.
Maybank currently holds a 69.05 per cent stake in the company.
The bank said the acquisition is expected to strengthen Maybank Ageas' position as a national insurance and takaful champion while providing greater flexibility to expand across Southeast Asia.
It said the proposed acquisition will deliver immediate profit after tax and minority interests, earnings per share and return on equity (ROE) accretion and will contribute to sustainable and resilient long-term value creation through durable earnings growth and higher ROE
Maybank said the purchase price of RM4.83 billion reflects a price-to-book multiple of 1.98 times and a price-to-earnings multiple of 15.3 times.
"Maybank will fund the proposed acquisition through a combination of internal and external funding sources," it said.
Its president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli said the acquisition marks a milestone in the group's efforts to drive the next phase of growth for its insurance and takaful business across Southeast Asia.
He said the bank will continue investing in innovation and digital capabilities to enhance productivity, lower operating costs and improve the customer experience.
"New and existing customers will also have access to expanded suite of solutions including enhanced product offerings.
"This is part of our strengthened commitment to improving accessibility and making insurance and takaful protection easier to be obtained by all consumers.
"Going forward, Maybank will continue to drive long term value creation for its shareholders, and owning Maybank Ageas fully is one of the initiatives for the aforesaid purpose," he said in a statement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina calls for agile legal framework amid AI and digital challenges
Article:
hakimmahari@nst.com.my
PUTRAJAYA: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation and cybersecurity threats require Malaysia's legal framework to become more agile, responsive and future-ready, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said the changing global landscape had created new challenges that required continuous improvements in laws and institutions.
She said legal reforms were no longer limited to introducing or amending legislation, but also involved ensuring public institutions remained trusted, effective and capable of responding to emerging challenges.
"Today, we are facing challenges that are very different and increasingly complex.
"The development of AI, digital transformation, cybersecurity threats and changes in the global landscape require a legal system that is more agile, responsive, relevant and prepared for the future," she said.
Azalina was speaking at the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) monthly assembly here today.
She said integrity, accountability and good governance must remain the foundation of every policy and reform undertaken by the government.
"Reform is not merely about producing new laws, but ensuring the benefits are truly felt by the people."
Azalina said several institutional reforms had already been implemented, including strengthening witness protection, amendments to laws involving child protection, and the implementation of the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 through the establishment of the Anti-Bullying Tribunal and advocacy programmes.
She said these efforts reflected the government's commitment to ensuring legal reforms translated into stronger protection and better public services.
Azalina added that reforms required close cooperation between departments and agencies, supported by a working culture based on collaboration, shared expertise and open communication.
She said the Legal Affairs Division would continue strengthening its capacity to address future challenges through improved governance and the use of technology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver and wife plead not guilty as Melaka court hears child abuse charges
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 3 — A 36-year-old lorry driver and his wife pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court in Ayer Keroh today to charges of physically abusing their nine-year-old daughter last month.
The accused were charged separately before Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah.
The victim’s biological father was accused of physically abusing his eldest daughter and causing injury to her at Taman 1 Krubong at around 7.00pm on July 19.
He was charged under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for a fine not exceeding RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nor Asnini Kamarudin offered bail of RM20,000 with an additional condition that the accused not interfere with prosecution witnesses, particularly the victim.
The man, who was unrepresented, requested that bail be reduced, citing his irregular income and the need to support his two school-going children.
The court then granted bail at RM10,000 with the additional conditions sought by the prosecution.
Meanwhile, the accused’s wife, aged 35, also pleaded not guilty to a charge of abusing the same victim at the same location, time and date.
She was charged under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a fine not exceeding RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Qayyum Ramlan offered bail of RM20,000 with the additional condition that the accused not interfere with prosecution witnesses, particularly the victim.
The housewife, however, applied for reduced bail on the grounds that she is unemployed and cares for their other two children, aged nine and six.
Judge Rohatul Akmar granted RM9,000 bail and set September 8 for the next mention of the case, as well as for the appointment of counsel. — Bernama

Title: Singaporean biker killed, two fellow riders hurt in crash involving Toyota Vellfire on North-South Expressway near Kulai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A 56-year-old Singaporean motorcyclist was killed and two Malaysian riders injured in a four-vehicle crash on the North-South Expressway near Kulai yesterday.
The collision, at KM44.6 of the southbound carriageway, involved a Toyota Vellfire and three high-powered motorcycles.
Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said preliminary investigations found that the three riders — the Singaporean and two Malaysians aged 57 and 39 — were travelling south when the crash occurred.
“The victim is believed to have lost control and crashed into the rear of the vehicle driven by a 32-year-old Singaporean woman, who was travelling in the right lane at the time.
“The incident also involved the other two motorcyclists. The victim was pronounced dead, while one of the other riders suffered a fractured right thigh and the other sustained minor injuries.
“We received information about the crash at 2.05pm,” he said in a statement.
The injured riders were taken to Temenggong Seri Maharaja Tun Ibrahim Hospital for treatment, while the Vellfire driver was unhurt.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Anyone with information has been asked to contact investigating officer Inspector Mohd Ruslan Mohamed at 013-3063710 or visit the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Kulai district police headquarters.

Title: State Speaker: Selangor assembly reviewing all lawmakers after bankruptcy disqualification claim
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 3 — The Selangor state assembly is reviewing the status of all its members after claims that one assemblyman may have been disqualified over bankruptcy,
Utusan Malaysia
reported today.
State assembly Speaker Lau Weng San said he could not yet confirm the identity of the lawmaker concerned because checks and investigations were still under way.
He said the review was being conducted under the Laws of the Constitution of Selangor before any conclusion was reached or decision made.
“We need to check because there are various possibilities. We have to conduct checks, and I will inform you once I receive the complete information.
“The review is taking time because checks are being carried out on various aspects,” he told the national daily during the second meeting of the fourth session of the 15th Selangor state assembly.
Utusan Malaysia
had earlier reported that the assembly was expected to clarify the status of a lawmaker alleged to have been disqualified over bankruptcy.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari previously said the matter would be determined by Lau before the Election Commission (EC) was informed.
Several assembly members were absent from their seats when the sitting began today, but Lau cautioned against assuming that any of them was the lawmaker referred to in the allegation.
“Whether it is true or not, we have to ask the person concerned. I cannot say or confirm anything. Being absent does not necessarily mean that the person has a problem, as alleged.
“That is up to the individual. We cannot force an assemblyman to attend. However, under the Laws of the Constitution of Selangor, if an assemblyman does not attend a sitting for six months without providing any official information, the seat must be vacated,” he said.
Lau said disqualification issues had arisen in previous terms, including in relation to the Kuang and Port Klang seats.
He added that Selat Klang assemblyman Datuk Abdul Rashid Asari and Meru assemblyman Mariam Abdul Rashid had previously submitted letters explaining their absence, including for medical leave.
“So, the fact that an assemblyman is absent does not necessarily mean that the person has a problem or is facing disqualification. Do not jump to conclusions or harbour suspicions.
“We are still carrying out checks, and it will take some time. We cannot make any assumptions,” he said.
Lau said any decision on whether to hold a by-election would rest with the EC.

Title: MetMalaysia alert: Torrential rain, lightning and gusty winds batter states from Kedah to Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected to affect eight states and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Sik and Baling in Kedah; Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Jeli, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan; and Besut, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu.
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Kuantan and Rompin in Pahang, as well as Kluang and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak and Sarawak, the affected areas are Kuching (Bau), Sri Aman, Betong (Pusa and Betong), Sarikei (Pakan, Julau and Meradong), Sibu and Kapit (Song and Kapit), and the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Keningau and Tambunan), the West Coast and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia targets rail cable theft with possible RM100,000 fines and 1,146 new CCTV cameras, Dewan Negara told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The government is finalising amendments to the rail transport law to impose heavier penalties with fines of up to RM100,000 on criminals who trespass and steal cables from national rail facilities.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the proposal to increase the fine from the current RM1,000 is expected to be tabled in the next Parliament session.
“We will amend this law to reach RM100,000 for each offence... currently in the process and God willing, perhaps by the end of this year in the next session, a stricter amendment to the law will be brought to this House,” he said during a question-and-answer session at Dewan Negara today.
He was responding to a question by Senator Datuk Mohd Hatta Md Ramli regarding the government’s mitigation measures to address travel disruptions due to cable theft and ensure public transport is guaranteed.
Hasbi said the amendment to the law was urgent as the existing penalties were deemed too lenient compared to the impact of damage and delays to train operations that the operators had to bear.
Additionally, the move was also driven by a surge in cable theft cases which recorded a total loss of RM50 million across the Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) network, Prasarana Malaysia Berhad and the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
According to Hasbi, a total of 71 cable theft cases were recorded along the ECRL project with an estimated loss of RM4.06 million, while 13 cases of theft and damage to equipment and other materials related to the system resulted in a loss of RM0.69 million.
“This brings the total loss to RM4.75 million. Although the ECRL is still in the construction phase and has not yet involved travel disruptions for users, the incident has the potential to affect the project implementation schedule, including installation, testing, commissioning and operational preparations,” he said.
To strengthen security control on the ground, Hasbi said the government is currently in the process of installing 1,146 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras along the railway line from Johor to the north of the country.
In addition, he said KTMB has also acquired 20 units of scrambler motorcycles for use by the Auxiliary Police to tighten 24-hour patrols, in addition to implementing physical controls such as closing high-security manholes and using sniffer dogs (K9). — Bernama

Title: Woman killed, son injured after Toyota Avanza crashes into guardrail in Kedah
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 3 — A woman was killed while her son was injured after the vehicle they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a roadside guardrail along Jalan Batu Pengasah in Durian Burung, near Padang Terap, today.
Padang Terap police chief Supt Mohd Anuar Junoh said the incident, which occurred at about 7.35am, claimed the life of the 55-year-old woman, who was seated in the front passenger seat. Her 21-year-old son, who was driving the Toyota Avanza, sustained bodily injuries.
“Preliminary investigations found that the victims were travelling from Kuala Nerang towards Durian Burung when the vehicle skidded onto the left road shoulder before crashing into the roadside guardrail.
“The woman, who was trapped in the vehicle, was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer, while her son was taken to hospital for further treatment. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, a Kedah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) spokesman said the department received an emergency call at 7.44am, and a team from the Kuala Nerang Fire and Rescue station arrived at the scene about 20 minutes later.
“Upon arrival, firefighters found a woman trapped in the front passenger seat, while the male driver had already been taken to hospital. The team successfully extricated the victim, who was later confirmed dead, and handed her body over to the police for further action.
“The firefighters also carried out clean-up work to remove broken glass and an oil spill from the accident scene. The operation concluded at 9.25am,” the spokesman said. — Bernama

Title: Cambodian DPM Prak Sokhonn arrives in Malaysia for two-day official visit
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 3 — Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Prak Sokhonn arrived in Malaysia today for a two-day official visit.
The visit is expected to inject fresh momentum into the robust partnership between the two countries.
Sokhonn and his delegation arrived at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 at 1.48pm on a commercial flight.
Also present to welcome Sokhonn at the airport were Cambodian Ambassador to Malaysia Ouk Chandara and the Malaysian Government’s chief ceremony officer Datuk Rozainor Ramli.
Sokhonn is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim before proceeding with his other official engagements.
